title: UK logistics vacancy eases in Q3 2026
fact: CBRE reported a UK logistics vacancy rate of 6.56% in Q3 2026, down from 7.1% at the end of Q2.
implication: Underwrite local submarkets individually. A strengthening headline does not remove lease-up risk, obsolete-stock capex or tenant concentration.
question: Which supply-constrained micro-locations create dependable occupancy and pricing resilience?

title: Mid-box transactions show resilience
fact: Savills reported 4.14 million sq ft of UK prime mid-box take-up across 83 transactions by the end of Q3 2026.
implication: Potential origination thesis for specialised mid-box logistics, but compare rent, vacancy, local land supply and asset age rather than treating aggregate take-up as a buy signal.
question: Could aggregation of occupied mid-box assets generate superior downside with refurbishment-led upside?

title: Heat network regulation has commenced
fact: Ofgem's regulatory oversight of heat networks began in January 2026, bringing the sector within a consumer-protection regulatory framework.
implication: The commercial thesis should account for governance, consumer outcomes, operations, reporting, compliance costs and operating capability—not just demand growth.
question: Which founder-led operators have the controls and delivery capabilities to scale under the new regulatory expectations?
source: Ofgem, heat networks regulation is now live

title: Future Homes and Buildings Standards published
fact: The government published changes to building regulations and statutory guidance on 24 March 2026, including routes for buildings connected to heat networks.
implication: Heat-network opportunities should be tested against housebuilder pipelines, planning, construction timelines, customer contracts and execution risk.
question: Can long-duration contracted heat infrastructure scale with verified delivery and installation capacity?

title: UK industrial policy continues to support clean energy deployment
fact: The UK's Modern Industrial Strategy identifies clean energy industries among the growth-driving priority sectors.
implication: Investment thesis needs to distinguish long-term policy direction from asset-level contracted revenue, counterparty risk and project deliverability.
question: Where is the deployment bottleneck operational, rather than technological, and suitable for an AssetCo–OpCo platform?
